source.title: The Lifecycle of the Spectral Edge: From Gradient Learning to Weight-Decay Compression

record.tranche_reason: The study tests grokking on two small sequence tasks and investigates its dynamics with spectral-edge measurements and weight-decay interventions, rather than reproducing the original modular-arithmetic setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking occurrence and timing but does not provide train/test accuracy curves or a training-set-size sweep. Its claims about the spectral edge are new measurements, not results cited from other work.
record.test_reason: The study trains small Transformers on two algorithmic or compositional sequence tasks (Dyck-1, SCAN), with and without weight decay, and reports whether and when grokking occurs. That bears on V1, and on V5's claim that weight decay is needed. Most of its results are spectral-edge measurements that no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the spectral edge moves from a gradient-driven learning phase to a weight-decay-driven compression phase at grokking, marked by gradient–weight-decay alignment. They conclude that weight decay drives post-grok compression and nonlinear re-encoding, not the persistence of generalization. They also report that grokking occurs only with weight decay, and say the alignment–grokking link is correlational.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Dyck-1 and SCAN tasks, and analyzes update-trajectory spectral edges, gradient/weight-decay decomposition, ablation, and post-grok weight-decay interventions rather than reproducing the original modular-arithmetic training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking occurrence differs between ω = 1 and ω = 0; the reported spectral-edge behavior also differs between Dyck and SCAN.

fits_no_version.finding: At grokking, the update energy along the top Gram direction flips from gradient-driven (97.6% Dyck, 88.7% SCAN) to weight-decay-driven (5.3%, 0.2% gradient).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking coincides with gradient and weight decay aligning along the dominant update direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the post-grok spectral edge sharply cuts accuracy, while random-subspace ablation has no effect. In SCAN the effect is larger for the grokked model than the memorized one.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The post-grok spectral edge is causally important despite flat curvature along it.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing weight decay after grokking keeps test accuracy (0.973 vs 0.982). It restores linear-probe R2 (0.99) and raises the parameter norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After grokking, weight decay drives representational compression but is not needed to keep generalization.

record.problems: Both evaluated tasks are small-scale (150K–1.5M parameters and 50–2048 training samples). The study does not show train/test accuracy curves or a training-set-size sweep for the grokking claim. The authors state that the gradient–weight-decay alignment evidence is correlational and that the decomposition has not been tested at the larger scale discussed in prior work.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Training accuracy saturating before test accuracy, a chance-to-near-perfect jump, and growth of the delay as the training set shrinks.
Circuit efficiency, a critical dataset size, and ungrokking below it.
No continuous progress measure anticipating the jump is reported here (the commutator lead times are cited from prior work). No removal of memorizing components is tracked.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale sweep.
Algorithms learned across runs or architectures are not compared.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The '24/24 with WD' figure includes modular-arithmetic runs cited from the author's thesis, so it should not be a row. The post-grok intervention holds dataset size fixed, so it cannot test V5's ungrokking prediction. Dyck and SCAN only, 150K–1.5M parameters. Single author, preprint.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report training-accuracy saturation, test accuracy at chance before grokking, the size of a test-accuracy jump, or how delay changes with training-set size.
The study does not track gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, or continuous progress measures anticipating a test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic image, text, or molecule task, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
The study tests weight decay's effects after grokking, but does not sweep dataset size, identify a critical dataset size, or test ungrokking below one.
Three seeds are reported, but the study does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs or architectures and hyperparameters.
The study does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits in the softmax as explanations for grokking.
